stances.quote:

stances.summary: Observes traders link Chinese bank recapitalization to debt creation and growth targets
stances.quote:
2/4
It's interesting (although not at all surprising) that the recapitalization of Chinese banks is interpreted by iron ore traders as something that will boost the price of iron ore. It shows that they understand the link that ties debt creation to political growth targets.

stances.quote:

stances.summary: Intra-system recapitalization ineffective against systemic financial risk
stances.quote:
5/8
When the banks themselves recapitalize each other, this improves safety only if the risk is that a few individual banks are overextended. If the whole system is overextended, the additional capital does no good at all.

stances.summary: Chinese banks undercapitalized relative to asset quality
stances.quote:
3/8
This is in principle good news because Chinese banks are seriously undercapitalized given the quality of their assets, and to encourage them to keep lending they need to expand their accounting capital.

stances.summary: Argues external capital sources reduce systemic financial risk
stances.quote:
4/8
The problem, as you learn (or should learn) in your basic finance course, is that while additional capital  improves the safety of the individual entity that receives it, it only improves the the safety of the overall financial system if it comes from outside that system.
